methodological_rigor.justification: Preclinical in vitro and mouse model study with comprehensive mechanistic characterization. Base-editing screens performed in primary human T cells from two donors; validation across multiple tumor models (Nalm6, neuroblastoma, mediastinal lymphoma) and in NSG mouse models. In vivo studies include longitudinal monitoring with bioluminescence imaging and comprehensive safety assessments (organ pathology, cytokine profiling, liver enzymes). Limitations: no formal sample size calculation for screening; preclinical data lacks human clinical validation; donor sample small (n=2 for initial screen).

clinical_relevance_loe.justification: Preclinical mechanistic study demonstrating proof-of-concept for CAR-adapted base editing optimization. Identified point mutations (E81K for 4-1BBz, L32P for 28z) improve T cell function across multiple tumor entities in mouse models without safety signals. Strong translational rationale for improving FDA-approved CAR T cell designs, but entirely preclinical without clinical trial data or human patient application.

reporting_quality.justification: Comprehensive preclinical reporting with detailed methods, supplementary tables, and clear figures. Screening methodology well-described with appropriate controls (CD19-KO neutral controls, RASA2-KO positive controls). Single-cell RNA-seq, metabolomics, and live-cell imaging methods thoroughly documented. Central pathology validation. However, no explicit statement regarding data/code availability or deposition of edited cell lines.

novelty_literature.justification: Novel ROADSTAR (Rational Optimization of Activation-Dependent Signaling Through Targeted Allelic Reprogramming) platform for systematically screening base-edited point mutations in CAR T cells. Identification of CAR design-specific mutations (E81K for 4-1BBz costimulation, L32P for CD28 costimulation) with opposing effects on PI3K signaling but complementary benefits addresses significant gap in precision CAR T engineering. Represents meaningful mechanistic advancement over prior non-context-specific base-editing screens.

writing_presentation.justification: Well-organized manuscript with clear presentation of complex genomic and cellular data. Methods section comprehensive with appropriate detail for reproducibility. Figures effectively communicate screening results, signaling pathway modulation, and in vivo efficacy. Discussion appropriately contextualizes findings relative to CAR design differences and prior optimization strategies. Publication-ready presentation.

key_strengths: Novel ROADSTAR base-editing screening platform demonstrating systematic identification of CAR design-specific mutations to optimize T cell function
Comprehensive mechanistic characterization including transcriptomics (scRNA-seq, bulk RNA-seq), metabolomics, and live-cell imaging revealing distinct signaling effects of E81K vs L32P
E81K-edited 4-1BBz CAR T cells show enhanced effector function with improved long-term persistence and superior tumor control across multiple tumor models without exhaustion
Rigorous in vivo safety validation showing no evidence of lymphomagenesis, aberrant T cell expansion, or cytokine release syndrome despite improved persistence
Applicability demonstrated across hematological and solid tumors using T cells from both healthy donors and chemotherapy-pretreated patients, supporting translational potential
key_concerns: Entirely preclinical study lacking human clinical data, clinical trial results, or human patient outcomes; mechanism of action based on mouse models may not fully predict efficacy in humans
Small sample size for initial screening (n=2 healthy donors); base-editing efficiencies modest (~50% for E81K, ~30% for L32P), raising clinical scalability concerns
No formal pre-specified hypothesis or sample size calculation for primary screening; statistical power of screen not formally justified
Limited comparison to other CAR T optimization strategies (shRNA knockdown, genetic KO, exogenous overexpression); unclear if base-editing approach offers advantages beyond precise dose calibration
Mouse models use single cell lines per tumor type and limited number of recipients (n=18-19 mice); generalizability to broader tumor heterogeneity unclear
Incomplete blinding: only tumor burden measurement blinded; treatment allocation not blinded in key in vivo experiments
chief_reviewer.rationale: Tier 4 assignment reflects novel preclinical discovery with solid mechanistic support through comprehensive multi-modal analyses and in vivo validation. However, entirely preclinical nature without clinical translation limits higher consideration. Appropriate for specialized oncology journal but requires clinical trial data for Tier 3+ recommendation.
